content:
Each move changes \(x+y\) by an odd amount, so after \(k\) moves, \(x+y\) has the same parity as \(k\). Since \(1991+1991=3982\) is even, \(k\) must be even.

Each move can increase \(x+y\) by at most \(3\), so
\[
k \ge \left\lceil \frac{3982}{3}\right\rceil = 1328.
\]
Since \(1328\) is even, this lower bound is possible.

Construct 1328 moves:
- \(662\) moves of \((1,2)\),
- \(665\) moves of \((2,1)\),
- \(1\) move of \((-1,2)\).

Then
\[
x = 662(1)+665(2)+1(-1)=1991,
\]
\[
y = 662(2)+665(1)+1(2)=1991.
\]
Thus the minimum number of moves is

\[
\boxed{1328}
\]
